Treasure Hunt

Four partnerships, four shared boards. Each third completed stage gives a key; every four keys unlock another chest.

Shared boards, separate partnerships

Pair with four partners. Each partnership advances its own shared board. Clearing a stage grants its stage rewards; stages 3, 6, 9, and so on also grant one key.

Completed stages in one slotTotal keys from that slot

Make a plan with your partners

  1. Ask when each partner can dig and agree on a realistic completed-stage target.
  2. Check all four boards before deciding where your remaining digs help most.
  3. Count total earned keys across the four slots. Chest thresholds are cumulative: 4, 8, 12, up to 32 keys.
A displayed stage is not necessarily completed. If you are still digging stage 7, enter stage 6 in a completed-stage planner.

Four-slot reward check

This projects eligible stage and chest rewards for one player. It assumes each eligible reward is claimed and excludes the initial Pickaxe grant.

Choose a dig with better odds

The solver eliminates arrangements that cross empty tiles or overlap confirmed treasures. Its percentages describe the chance of a tile containing an undiscovered treasure under an equal-valid-layout model.

Record every tile revealed in-game, including free reveals from bombs. The solver needs the resulting empty or treasure information, not a separate bomb simulation.

Open Treasure Hunt Solver

Bombs, moles and digging costs

Bombs can appear randomly and remove extra tiles.
A mole can appear randomly. Tap it immediately to receive Pinballs before it disappears.
